messages:
maia: Heads up — after the kernel swap to 0.10.2 we saw P95 jump ~35% on long-seq workloads. I profiled a few traces and there are two things that stand out: a) memcpy hotspots during KV cache miss handling, b) increased tail cost in batch completion when a single long request stalls the microbatch. Thinking we should try per-model token ceilings + a short probation admit window so long requests don't block small ones.

arpit: +1. Do you have numbers for token budget vs observed throughput?

maia: Quick numbers from the run (mixed Llama/OPT models): P50=28ms -> 26ms, P95=210ms -> 285ms after kernel swap. KV miss rate up from 6% -> 9% on the dataset that spikes long prefs. Average tokens/batch rose 12% which amplifies serialization cost.

jonathan: I captured a flame snippet. The big goroutines are memcpy + serialize_kv for misses, and the batch assembler waits 8–12ms for the last request in the window. We may need to tighten batch formation TTL for high-variance queues.

lia: Related: what if we add an "early-finalize" heuristic — when a large request is the tail, create a "mini-batch" for the remaining queued small items after X ms. That avoids punishing short requests.

maia: Exactly. Proposed experiment:
1) Per-model admit token ceiling: cap tokens_in_flight per model (configurable, default 16k tokens)
2) Probation window for new long sequences: first M requests treated with stricter ceiling for 30s
3) Early-finalize TTL: if head request > Y tokens and waiting > Z ms, flush a mini-batch for other queued requests
4) 429 policy change: respond with Retry-After when ceiling reached, and expose soft-reject header "X-Soft-Reject: admission-ceiling" so clients can adapt

arpit: Sounds good. Two operational questions: what are safe defaults for ceilings and how do we rollback fast if we see regression?

maia: Defaults I tested in staging: ceiling=16000 tokens, probation M=3, early-finalize TTL=6ms, Y=1024 tokens, Z=6ms. Rollback: feature flag on admission controller with traffic split and immediate disable via console; deploy-bot can also revert kernel.

perfbot: perfcheck: staging run with proposed settings (50k requests) -> P95 reduced 20% compared to current kernel-0.10.2 baseline; KV miss tail down 12%.

jonathan: One caveat: kernel selection hysteresis. If we flip back to older kernel for some model variants, admission rules must respect kernel capability (e.g., older kernels have slower memcpy paths). We should add kernel index in the admission scoreboard to pick conservative ceilings per kernel-version + model combo.

lia: Agreed. Also think about jittering requeue delay so when we send 429+Retry-After we don't get thundering retry storms. Randomize 0..200ms on top of Retry-After.

arpit: For observability, add metrics: admit_ceiling_hits, admit_ceiling_rejections, early_finalize_events, per-model-token-inflight_gauge, and a histogram of Retry-After seen by clients.

maia: I'll open an experiment branch and a short checklist for QA:
- Run synthetic mixes with heavy short/long skew (70/30)
- Measure P50/P95 per-model and KV miss tail
- Validate headers returned on rejections and no hard 503s in steady state
- Smoke rollback path

deploy-bot: deploy job 4867 finished to staging (branch: admission-experiments).

jonathan: One more thought — for the mini-batch flush, make kernel hints: prefer kernels that have fast small-batch startup for those mini-batches, else skip flush. We can encode that as a kernel_capabilities boolean: "fast_small_batch_start".

maia: Good call. I'll add kernel_capabilities to the admission config map and default conservative when unknown. Running the A/B tomorrow at 9:30 PT — will post results here.

lia: :thumbsup: If perfbot sees regressions after the A/B, let's pause and revert admission changes before touching kernel.

maia: Agreed. Will drop results and flame graphs in this thread after the run.
